source_refs.note: Exercise 9.2, Question 7: book page 176 (PDF 181); its answer is key entry 8 on PDF 307 (response not zero at t = 4; 'in' for 'is'); checked with sympy and the solution book (PDF 864-865).

blocks.prompt: 7. Given a signal represented by \(Q(t) = t^3 - 6t^2 + 11t - 6\), determine if the system response is zero at \(t = 4\). If so, identify the factor.
blocks.explanation:
The response at \(t = 4\) is \(Q(4)\); it is zero exactly when \(t - 4\) is a factor (Factor Theorem).
We must say yes or no, and name the factor if yes.
Plan: work out \(Q(4)\); zero means factor \(t - 4\), otherwise no such factor.
steps:
Given: \(Q(t) = t^3 - 6t^2 + 11t - 6\), input \(t = 4\).
To find: whether \(Q(4) = 0\), and if so the factor.
Method: Factor Theorem: \(t - 4\) is a factor of \(Q(t)\) exactly when \(Q(4) = 0\).

Draw the conclusion
\[Q(4) = 6 \neq 0\]
Why: The response at \(t = 4\) is 6, not zero, so by the Factor Theorem \(t - 4\) is not a factor and there is no factor to identify.

Check by synthetic division by \(t - 4\)
Coefficients \(1,\ -6,\ 11,\ -6\), \(a = 4\):
bring down 1; \(1 \times 4 = 4\), \(-6 + 4 = -2\);
\(-2 \times 4 = -8\), \(11 - 8 = 3\);
\(3 \times 4 = 12\), \(-6 + 12 = 6\).
\[\text{Remainder} = 6 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Same remainder 6. For interest, \(Q(1) = Q(2) = Q(3) = 0\), so \(Q(t) = (t - 1)(t - 2)(t - 3)\): the response is zero only at \(t = 1, 2, 3\), and a cubic has at most three zeros.
blocks.final_answer: No. \(Q(4) = 6 \neq 0\), so the response is not zero at \(t = 4\) and \(t - 4\) is not a factor.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: In the answer key (PDF 307) this question's answer is printed as entry 8, "System response in not zero when \(t = 4\)" ("in" is a misprint for "is"). It agrees with our working; the key numbers are shifted because it has 10 entries for 7 printed questions.
